lede: The story of Christmas in DeSoto starts in the 1840s, when the Parks, Cheshier, Ramsey and Johnson families settled here and T. J. Johnson built a general store in 1848, and today it centers on the city's Home for the Holidays series at the Aquatic and Recreation Center at McCowan Park. DeSoto has 6 events on this page, from the Hometown Holiday Marketplace on December 5, 2026 to the chamber music concert on December 18.
sections: Four families and a store called the Store

The Handbook of Texas says DeSoto was founded in the 1840s by the Parks, Cheshier, Ramsey and Johnson families, with Parks thought to be first. The Ramseys' daughter Mary, born in 1846, was reportedly the first White child born west of the Trinity. In 1848 T. J. Johnson built the first general store at the junction of what became Belt Line and Hampton roads, and the place became known as the Store. A post office opened in 1884 and was named DeSoto, either for Hernando De Soto or for a local resident, Dr. Thomas Hernando DeSoto Stewart. The post office stayed in service until 1906.
From a crossroads to a city of commuters

DeSoto had seven businesses and 97 people in 1930. It incorporated in 1949, and as Dallas expanded south the town became a city of commuters, with an estimated 90 percent of its workforce traveling to jobs in Dallas or Grand Prairie. The Handbook of Texas lists 1,969 residents in 1960, 6,617 in 1970, 15,538 in 1980 and 37,646 in 2000. The Texas Almanac gives 56,145 for 2020. The Handbook also lists thirty-seven public parks, a library, three fire stations and ten public schools among its civic facilities.
Home for the Holidays at McCowan Park

The City of DeSoto fills two Saturdays at the Aquatic and Recreation Center, 1400 Academy Way, from 10 am to 2 pm. The Hometown Holiday Marketplace comes first on December 5, 2026, and Furry Family Holiday Photos follows on December 12, run with the Tri-City Animal Shelter and Adoption Center. The city calendar lists photos with Santa, train rides, hot cocoa, letters to Santa, face painting and food trucks on both days, and both have free Eventbrite tickets. On Friday, December 18, from 7 to 9 pm, the Cultural Arts Department presents a free chamber music concert, An Evening of Elegance, at the Corner Theater.
trains: DeSoto began as a crossroads store in 1848, and the Handbook of Texas says it grew as a commuter city serving Dallas. DART's Blue Line runs from Downtown Rowlett to UNT Dallas Station, and the Red Line runs from Parker Road Station in Plano to Westmoreland Station in Dallas. The city's own Home for the Holidays days include train rides at the Aquatic and Recreation Center. For a bigger train outing, the Interurban Railway Museum is in Plano, the Museum of the American Railroad is in Frisco and the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley runs in Dallas.

kidfact: DeSoto's first general store, built in 1848, was so important that the whole neighborhood was simply called the Store.
faq: How did DeSoto get its name?

The post office opened in 1884 and was named DeSoto. The Handbook of Texas says the name honors either the explorer Hernando De Soto or a local resident, Dr. Thomas Hernando DeSoto Stewart. The community itself had been founded in the 1840s and was known earlier as the Store, after a general store built in 1848.

The Handbook of Texas lists the Parks, Cheshier, Ramsey and Johnson families as founders in the 1840s, with Parks thought to be the first. T. J. Johnson built the first general store in 1848, and in 1850 Otway B. Nance built a farm that eventually became a Texas historic landmark.
How did DeSoto grow into a city?

DeSoto incorporated in 1949 with about 300 people in 1950. As Dallas expanded south it became a commuter city, with an estimated 90 percent of workers commuting to Dallas or Grand Prairie. The Handbook of Texas lists 6,617 residents in 1970 and 37,646 in 2000, and the Texas Almanac lists 56,145 for 2020.
What is DeSoto's Home for the Holidays series?

Home for the Holidays is the City of DeSoto's run of holiday events. On December 5 and 12, 2026, the Aquatic and Recreation Center at McCowan Park hosts the Hometown Holiday Marketplace and Furry Family Holiday Photos, with Santa photos, train rides, hot cocoa, letters to Santa and face painting listed on the city calendar.
Is there a free holiday concert in DeSoto?

Yes. The City of DeSoto Cultural Arts Department presents An Evening of Elegance, Sounds of the Season, a chamber music concert, on Friday, December 18, 2026, from 7 to 9 pm at the Corner Theater, 211 E Pleasant Run Rd. The city calendar lists it as free to the public.
